rulings.challenge_claim: Two convergent items. (1) The front seam at Jer.49.19 rests on a fresh poetic image alone: no tier-1 device stands at the onset and no parashah mark falls at the Jer.49.18|Jer.49.19 edge, and the medium confidence never engages that gap. (2) The stated grammatical ground for not cutting at the setumah recorded at MT 49:19 -- that the lion simile's rhetorical questions run past the verse boundary into Jer.49.20-Jer.49.21 -- is contradicted by the verse bytes.
rulings.grounds: Both items verify. They are DISTINCT defects converging on one weakness: the first attacks the seam this unit draws, the second the ground on which it declines the seam inside its span. Item 1. Jer.49.19 opens הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה (oshb:Jer.49.19, byte tier), a presentative plus simile. The verse belongs to none of the three word-event shapes, stands among neither the six lamed-initial nation headers nor the four non-lamed header shapes, carries no koh-amar, no vocative and no imperative, and is absent from the 19 classified date-candidate sites -- so no tier-1 device stands at the onset. In the parashah layer (tier-3 weak, single-witness) the entries in and around the span are setumah keyed to MT 49:11, MT 49:19 and MT 49:22; the MT 49:19 entry trails that verse and therefore sits INSIDE the span, between its first and second verses, and nothing is keyed to MT 49:18, so the front edge carries no mark either. observed_substrate_signals records a refrain key only, which under the ruled granularity is texture, not an onset class. Item 2. The question series terminates inside Jer.49.19: וּמִי זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Jer.49.19, byte tier) closes at the verse-final accent, and Jer.49.20 opens לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.20, byte tier) -- a consequential particle plus second-person-plural imperative beginning an independent clause, the voice turning from first-person divine speech to speech about Yahweh in the third person. The second witness agrees, closing its quotation at the end of the verse and carrying “Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Edom” (web:Jer.49.20) outside it. The sentence-continuation ground is byte-false at both witnesses. NEW FINDING, which inverts the two items against each other: the seam this unit declines at Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 carries a hear-imperative of the same shape the ruled granularity names as a tier-1 internal seam class, plus the tier-3 setumah, while the seam it draws at Jer.49.18|Jer.49.19 carries neither. The disposition can still survive, but only on the ground the unit already holds elsewhere: the same two-verse template stands at Jer.49.19-Jer.49.20 and at Jer.50.44-Jer.50.45, and this tiling reads Jer.50.44-Jer.50.46 as one unit, so cutting at Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 would force the parallel cut there. SECOND NEW FINDING, on the recurrence digits: the leading identical run is 9 whitespace tokens at Jer.49.19 against Jer.50.44 (byte tier; diverging at the tenth, plene against defective, with a variant note carried at MT 50:44 and none at MT 49:19) and 7 whitespace tokens at Jer.49.20 against Jer.50.45 (byte tier; diverging at the nation name), counted on the maqaf-free staged extract -- the challenge's 7 and 6 name the right object under a maqaf-joined unit and understate it. THIRD NEW FINDING: both parashah citations here carry neither the single-witness nor the tier-3 label the Prophets rule requires on every citation.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the clause asserting that the lion simile's rhetorical questions continue grammatically past Jer.49.19 into Jer.49.20-Jer.49.21, and delete the matching clause in strongest_rejected_alternative asserting that the sentence the mark falls inside continues past the verse boundary; both are byte-false. Replace the warrant with the parallel-treatment ground the unit already carries, stated with its tier and unit: the same template opens Jer.49.19-Jer.49.20 and Jer.50.44-Jer.50.45, byte-identical for the leading 9 and 7 whitespace tokens respectively, and this tiling reads Jer.50.44-Jer.50.46 as one unit. In boundary_rationale, disclose that no tier-1 device stands at Jer.49.19 and that no parashah entry is keyed to MT 49:18, and add the single-witness and tier-3 labels to both parashah citations. Re-rate confidence against that disclosure. CURE TEST: the rewritten boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative must survive a read of Jer.49.19 and Jer.49.20 side by side -- the sentence-continuation claim that failed must not reappear in any form, and the restated warrant must apply symmetrically at Jer.50.44|Jer.50.45. Any change to the span itself, including adopting the Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 cut, is a PROPOSAL for owner adoption, not author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: The variant note at MT 49:25 is misidentified as sitting on a demonstrative; the header is called a different shape from its chapter neighbours when it is the same lamed-plus-nation form; and a paseq seg recorded inside the span at MT 49:24 goes undisclosed while the span's other scribal-layer object is named.
rulings.grounds: All three verify, and a fourth disclosure gap sits beside them. Variant object: the single note at MT 49:25 rides on the praise noun, not on a demonstrative -- עִ֣יר תהלה תְּהִלָּ֑ת (oshb:Jer.49.25, byte tier) sets the unpointed written form beside the pointed construct read form, and no demonstrative stands anywhere in that verse at any tier. Header form: לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק (oshb:Jer.49.23, byte tier) is the same lamed-plus-nation shape as לֶאֱד֗וֹם (oshb:Jer.49.7, byte tier) and לְקֵדָ֣ר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), and the header census carries all three among its six lamed-initial nation headers; what actually separates this site from its chapter neighbours is the absent speech formula, which the same sentence states correctly -- so only the form-class word is wrong, and the substrate keeps that class separate. The absence claim itself checks out: no koh-amar and no asher-hayah construction stands anywhere in the span (sweep: 0 verses in span, against 153 koh-amar verses book-wide). Disclosure: one paseq seg is recorded at MT 49:24, inside the span, and is never mentioned, while the variant at MT 49:25 is; the span-relevant mark-disclosure sweep is unconditional and does not stop at the objects the prose already found interesting. NEW FINDING: neither parashah citation here -- the front-seam entry keyed to MT 49:22 and the closing entry keyed to MT 49:27, both correctly typed setumah and correctly located -- carries the single-witness or tier-3 label, though the paseq convention used in the neighbouring units does carry it.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'a ketiv/qere note on the demonstrative at Jer.49.25' with the correct object -- one variant note at MT 49:25 on the praise noun, written form against read form, single-witness. Replace 'of a different shape than its neighbors' with the accurate discrimination: the same lamed-initial header form as the Ammon, Edom and Kedar headers, distinguished not by shape but by carrying no speech formula in the header verse or anywhere in Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27. Add the undisclosed paseq at MT 49:24 (1 seg, single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted). Add single-witness and tier-3 labels to both parashah citations. CURE TEST: read Jer.49.25 for a demonstrative before rewriting -- there is none, which is the test the original failed; and the completed disclosure must account for EVERY mark-layer entry inside Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, not only the one already named.

rulings.challenge_claim: The header verse is described as dating a coming strike, and literature_type_guess calls the unit dated, when the verse's relative clause is retrospective in both witnesses, the verse carries no date element, and it is absent from the book's classified date-site census; a residual sole-site exclusivity claim also ships without its own digit-bearing sweep.
rulings.grounds: Verified on every leg. The clause is אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), rendered “which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck” (web:Jer.49.28) -- a backward-looking identification of the target by a strike already inflicted, not a forward-looking date. No year, reign or month element stands in the verse at any tier, and the verse is absent from the 19 classified date-candidate sites; inside the nations block the classified date sites are Jer.46.2 and Jer.51.59. The comparandum sharpens it: the Egypt header carries the identical relative-clause construction אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכָּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.46.2, byte tier) AND, separately, the date element בִּשְׁנַת֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית (oshb:Jer.46.2, byte tier) -- exactly the element this header lacks, so the construction the unit read as dating is demonstrably not the dating element even where a date is present. The 'dates the coming strike' sentence and the 'dated' word in the type guess are therefore one byte-false claim with one cure. The residual verifies too: the sole-site wording is an exclusivity claim shipped with no digit-bearing sweep beside it, and the standing rule never lets a tier label or an accurate underlying fact substitute for that sweep; the fact does hold -- the plene byform stands at 1 verse against 29 for the dominant resh-family spelling -- and the rationale's 'the majority of this name's occurrences' is likewise an undigited quantity. NOT DISTURBED, because they re-verify from bytes: both variant descriptions (the added vav standing immediately before the final resh at MT 49:28, and against-them corrected to against-you at MT 49:30), the paseq at MT 49:28 handled count-only with no intra-verse position asserted, and the front-seam entry keyed to MT 49:27. NEW FINDING: that front-seam parashah citation carries no single-witness or tier-3 label although the paseq citation in the same sentence does -- an asymmetry inside one field.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'The same verse dates the coming strike to Nebuchadnezzar' with the retrospective reading -- the header identifies its target by a strike already inflicted, and the verse carries no date element of any shape. literature_type_guess: strike the word 'dated'. device_notes: give the sole-site claim its own digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit (plene resh-family byform: 1 verse; dominant resh-family spelling: 29 verses) and replace 'the majority of this name's occurrences' with that digit. Add single-witness and tier-3 labels to the parashah citation. CURE TEST: the rewritten fields fail if any date word remains attached to Jer.49.28 -- check the verse for a year, reign or month token and against the classified date-site census before writing, and confirm the retrospective reading against the second witness's rendering, which is the test the original failed. CORPUS-WIDE ORDER CANDIDATE: the same date word attaches to the lamed-headed sites at Jer.49.1 and Jer.49.7; sweep the date label across every header unit of the nations block as one order rather than site by site -- but EXCLUDE Jer.49.34, where the accession dating clause is byte-present.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two convergent items. (1) The seam actually drawn at Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32 carries no device in any layer, while strongest_rejected_alternative defends a different location, Jer.49.30, which is interior to the preceding unit and is not a seam anywhere in this tiling; the high confidence engages neither gap. (2) The opening sentence's claim that the material continues without an addressee shift is contradicted at that seam, where second-person-plural imperative address gives way to third-person report.
rulings.grounds: Both verify. They are the SAME core defect -- an unwarranted seam defended from the wrong location -- with a distinct byte finding attached to the second item. The substrate is silent at the seam: Jer.49.32 opens וְהָי֨וּ גְמַלֵּיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.49.32, byte tier) -- no speech formula, no header of the lamed or non-lamed class, no word-event shape, no date element, no vocative, no imperative; no parashah entry falls between the setumah keyed to MT 49:27 and the setumah keyed to MT 49:33; and no variant note and no paseq seg falls at MT 49:31 or MT 49:32. The rejected alternative's two discriminators -- the change of named target to Hazor and the renewed flight command -- both stand at Jer.49.30, interior to Jer.49.28-Jer.49.31, so the field's warrant addresses a boundary this tiling does not draw while the boundary it does draw is left unwarranted. The distinct byte finding: Jer.49.31 opens ק֣וּמוּ עֲל֗וּ (oshb:Jer.49.31, byte tier) against ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier) -- direct second-person-plural imperative address bracketing Jer.49.28-Jer.49.31 -- and Jer.49.32 drops that address for third-person report closing on the divine formula. NEW FINDING, a tier correction on that comparandum: each splice is byte tier at its own verse, but the RECURRENCE between them is accent_stripped and skeleton tier, not byte -- the two accent patterns differ -- so the bracket must be cited at the tier it actually reaches. On either available reading -- an undisclosed change of address at the seam, or no device at the seam at all -- the opening sentence is false and a high confidence rating with frontier_flag_considered false cannot stand.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: strike 'The spoils continue without an addressee shift' -- the imperative address standing at Jer.49.31 does not continue into Jer.49.32 -- and state what, if anything, stands at Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32, disclosing that no tier-1 device and no mark-layer entry falls there. strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite so its warrant addresses the seam actually drawn; a discriminator located at Jer.49.30 cannot license a cut at Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32. confidence: lower from high, and set frontier_flag_considered true. If the Jer.49.28|Jer.49.31 imperative bracket is cited, cite it at accent_stripped or skeleton tier, not byte. Add single-witness and tier-3 labels to the parashah citation. CURE TEST: the replacement warrant must be located AT Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32 and checkable there -- it fails if any verse other than Jer.49.31 or Jer.49.32 supplies it, which is exactly the test the original failed. Respanning -- to Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33 entire, or to a cut at Jer.49.29|Jer.49.30 where the discriminators actually sit -- is a PROPOSAL for owner adoption, not author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: The dating gloss romanizes the royal name in the long form where the verse writes the short one, and strongest_rejected_alternative's statement that the header carries no content of its own apart from the judgment contradicts this unit's own reading of the dating clause as the header's distinguishing feature; severity given as low.
rulings.grounds: Both defects are real and byte-confirmed; the severity is wrong and one framing point needs correcting. The verse writes בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַלְכ֛וּת צִדְקִיָּ֥ה (oshb:Jer.49.34, byte tier) -- the SHORT royal-name form, attested at 4 verses in this book against 44 for the long form -- and the unit romanizes it in the long form twice, in boundary_rationale and again in device_notes, inside the one claim whose entire value is byte-exact form discrimination, in a book where that name's spelling split is a catalogued sweep-hazard class. The contradiction verifies as well: the dating clause is content of the header's own, and the rationale itself treats it as the header's distinguishing feature. REFINEMENT 1, severity: this is not a low. A form-class fidelity error inside the unit's own discrimination claim belongs to the same class as the misnamed variant object and misnamed header form graded medium at the neighbouring units, and two independent byte-confirmed defects on one row confirm the grade; severity raised to medium. REFINEMENT 2, framing: the declared heuristic disposition on that sentence HOLDS on the axis it was tested against -- the wording is not an unswept exclusivity claim -- and that axis never tests substantive consistency, so both readings stand and only the second is a defect; the cure is to fix the sentence, not to relabel the flag. EXPLICITLY NOT DISTURBED, and important not to sweep: the word 'dated' is CORRECT here. The accession dating clause stands in this verse's own bytes and the header census records this site as dated -- a different object from the byte-false date labels attached to the chapter's lamed-headed sites. Everything else re-verifies: the four-site asher-hayah nations-header shape, the malkhut form as a different noun form from the three mamlekhet/mamlekhut construct sites, the variant on the nation name at MT 49:36, the two paseq segs at MT 49:37 with their single-witness label, the front-seam entry keyed to MT 49:33, and all splices at byte tier. NEW FINDING: that parashah citation carries no single-witness or tier-3 label although the paseq citation two sentences away does.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and device_notes: replace both occurrences of the long-form romanization with the short form the verse writes, and name the form -- short royal-name spelling, 4 verses book-wide against 44 for the long form. strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite so it stops denying the header the content the rationale relies on; the case for keeping header and declaration together rests on the declaration completing the header's sense, not on the header being empty. Add single-witness and tier-3 labels to the parashah citation. CURE TEST: read the romanization back against the verse's own bytes letter by letter -- the cure fails if the written name and the romanized name differ in any letter, which is the test the original failed. Do NOT apply the nations-block date-label sweep to this unit: the dating clause here is byte-present and the label is correct.

rulings.challenge_claim: The two variant pairs are labelled the restoration idiom's own two verbs when the second is the noun the verb governs; and the parashah entry adduced as corroborating the front seam trails this unit's single verse, so it bears on the back seam instead. Sub-claims in the same item: a four-note verse is not itself a doubled-note site; and the parallel idiom is invoked with no quoted form and no tier.
rulings.grounds: The headline claim verifies on both legs; one sub-claim is refuted and one residual is stronger than stated. Form class: the object marker settles it -- אֶת שבית שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.39, byte tier) puts the second variant pair immediately after the marker, as the NOUN the preceding verb governs, and the same construction without variants at the Ammon coda, אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier), shows it unambiguously; with no morphology layer staged, a form-class label of that reach is a byte-checkable claim and the bytes refuse it. Note the boundary_rationale wording is clean -- it names each written form against each read form without calling them verbs -- so the defect sits in device_notes alone. Mark direction: the setumah is keyed to MT 49:39, so it trails this unit's only verse and can corroborate only the back seam at Jer.49.39|Jer.50.1, never the front seam at Jer.49.38|Jer.49.39 that the sentence claims for it; the Ammon parallel has the identical geometry, its entry keyed to MT 49:6 with nothing at MT 49:5, so it cannot supply the missing front-seam corroboration either. REFUTED sub-claim, and it needs no cure: the objection that a four-note verse is not itself a doubled-note site does not hold. The variant census defines a closed class of TWELVE doubled-note verses and names MT 50:11 among them at 4 notes, beside MT 50:6 at 2 and this unit's own verse at 2; the sentence uses that class exactly and parenthesizes the four-note count besides, so it is precise rather than misleading. REFINED residual, the most useful correction here: the Ammon idiom is indeed invoked with no quoted form and no tier, and the recurrence is byte tier -- but on the READ side only. The run אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier) is byte-identical to the corresponding run at this unit's verse under both read forms, while the written forms differ at both tokens; the identity is qere-borne, which is exactly what a doubled-note site obliges the prose to disclose. One point flagged and NOT decided, because it is owner-level: whether the latter-days temporal frame counts as a fresh tier-1 onset is what licenses the closure formula ending Jer.49.38 to close under the ruled closure-corroboration-only treatment; it stands neither among the enumerated onset classes nor excluded from them, and that reading governs this unit's confidence.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace 'the restoration idiom's own two verbs' with the correct form classes -- the verb, and the object noun it governs standing after the object marker -- and add the recurrence tier with its condition: byte-identical to the run at Jer.49.6 under the READ forms only, the written forms differing at both tokens. boundary_rationale: re-anchor the parashah sentence so the entry keyed to MT 49:39 corroborates the back seam at Jer.49.39|Jer.50.1, and state that no mark-layer entry falls at the front seam at Jer.49.38|Jer.49.39; add the single-witness and tier-3 labels. confidence: lower from high, since the front seam's only signal is the content pivot plus the temporal frame. LEAVE UNCHANGED: the doubled-note comparison at Jer.50.6 and Jer.50.11 -- it matches the census class and its counts exactly. CURE TEST: the corrected form-class sentence must survive a read-back against the object marker standing in the verse, and the re-anchored mark sentence must name WHICH seam the entry sits on -- the two tests the original failed. ROUTE TO THE OWNER, not the author wave: whether a latter-days temporal frame is a fresh tier-1 onset for closure-formula purposes.

rulings.challenge_claim: Convergent on one defect: the curly-quoted English at Jer.50.2 runs through the first god-name while the Hebrew splice beside it stops at the city name -- and the splice additionally opens on an imperative the gloss does not render, so the extents diverge in both directions. Attached and distinct: the tier-3 layer cited at the front seam runs unstated across this unit's own back seam; the nations header at Jer.49.34 is described as just closed when it opens its unit; and the sentence carrying the front-seam disclosure is malformed.
rulings.grounds: The convergent core is one and the same defect, and the two-directional statement is the accurate one. The splice is אִמְרוּ֩ נִלְכְּדָ֨ה בָבֶ֜ל (oshb:Jer.50.2, byte tier); the god-name material the gloss reaches sits in the next two words, הֹבִ֥ישׁ בֵּל֙ (oshb:Jer.50.2, byte tier), outside the splice; and the imperative opening the splice goes unrendered in the gloss. So the gloss covers what the splice does not AND the splice covers what the gloss does not, against the standing rule that gloss extent equals splice extent. The three attached items verify as well. The parashah entries keyed to MT 49:39 and MT 50:5 leave MT 50:1 through MT 50:4 unmarked, so the segment opening after MT 49:39 does run across this unit's back seam at Jer.50.3|Jer.50.4 while the same layer is cited at the front seam. REFINEMENT there: that is a cross-seam cohesion disclosure, not a failure of the symmetry sweep -- no mark-layer entry falls inside Jer.50.1-Jer.50.3, so the span-relevant sweep owes nothing, and at tier-3 single-witness the absence is never counterevidence in either direction; the cure is a sentence, not a boundary. The header at Jer.49.34 does OPEN its own unit, whose material closes at Jer.49.39, so 'just closed at Jer.49.34' misplaces it; and the sentence opening 'This Jer.49.39, the Elam restoration coda' is malformed as written. NOT DISTURBED, because they re-verify: the davar-asher-dibber header shape at Jer.50.1, recorded in the header census as its own non-lamed shape and correctly held apart from the three word-event shapes and from the nations-header shape at Jer.49.34; the summons splice matching its gloss exactly; and the front-seam entry keyed to MT 49:39. NEW FINDING: that front-seam parashah citation carries neither the single-witness nor the tier-3 label.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss so its extent equals the splice's -- either narrow the curly-quoted English to the words the splice covers, INCLUDING the imperative it opens on, or extend the splice through the god-name material the gloss already reaches; one edit, not two half-edits. Repair the malformed sentence opening 'This Jer.49.39', and replace 'just closed at Jer.49.34' with the header's actual role -- it opens its unit, whose material closes at Jer.49.39. Add one sentence recording that no mark-layer entry falls inside Jer.50.1-Jer.50.3 and that the segment opening after MT 49:39 runs past this unit's back seam, disclosed as tier-3 weak and single-witness and NOT as counterevidence in either direction; add the single-witness and tier-3 labels to the front-seam citation. CURE TEST: set the rewritten gloss beside the splice token for token -- the cure fails if either side reaches a word the other does not, which is the test the original failed.
